data.body:
CORRECTION to the preceding triage: "CONSEQUENCE B — TEST DEFECT" overstated it. NO J11 TEST
CHANGE IS NEEDED.

I wrote that the inbound cell "must drive by an available TRANSITION name and assert the
destination the server itself declares". That was the right remedy for the OLD transport contract.
With [rebar:7f93-2743-a597-4f98]'s fix (Gerrit 1202) a destination STATUS name is now a legitimate
argument — resolution tries an exact transition-name match first, then a unique `to.name` match —
so `_in_status`'s existing `transition_issue_by_name(key, "In Progress")` becomes correct usage
rather than a misuse, and it will resolve via `Start Progress`.

So BOTH transition-status cells (inbound and outbound) should go green on the ONE product fix,
with no edit to `test_dc_mutations.py`. That is the better outcome and worth stating plainly: the
inbound cell was not wrong, it was ahead of the contract — it passed the value the rest of the
codebase passes (`LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA`'s workflow-state name), and the transport was the piece
that did not honour it.

WHAT TO VERIFY ON THE NEXT HARNESS RUN, rather than assume: that
`test_inbound_mutation_round_trips[04-transition-status]` reaches its ORACLE at all. Its previous
failure was an uncaught `ValueError` during setup, so the inbound status path has never actually
been exercised end to end — a pass will be its first real evidence, and a NEW failure mode there
(e.g. the local ticket not picking up the status) would be a genuine, previously-hidden finding
rather than a regression.
